book.title: The Virginian: A Horseman of the Plains
book.author: Owen Wister

underline.instructions: `chapter` is a passage of a novel. What would a reader mark in it to keep?
criteria: A reader would mark nothing in this passage
A reader might mark a sentence of this passage for what it says
A reader would mark a sentence of this passage for how it is said
A reader would copy out more than one sentence of this passage, for how they are said

draft.instructions: `chapter` is a passage of a novel. What does it read like?

criteria.first: A first draft, written fast and not gone over
criteria.worked: A text gone over until it was clean
criteria.finished: A text in which every word has been weighed

editor.instructions: `chapter` is a passage of a novel. What would a good editor do with it?

memory.instructions: `chapter` is a passage of a novel. A week after reading it, what would a reader remember of it?

criteria.image: An image or a phrase from it

slush.instructions: `chapter` is a passage of a novel. Sent to a publisher today with no name on it, what would become of the book it is from?

criteria.rejected: It would be turned down within a page
criteria.read: It would be read with interest and turned down

anyone.instructions: `chapter` is a passage of a novel. Who could have written it?
criteria: Anyone who writes could have written this passage
A competent professional could have written this passage
Only a writer with a manner of their own could have written this passage

lesson.instructions: `chapter` is a passage of a novel. Would a teacher of writing give it to a class as an example to learn from?

warning.instructions: `chapter` is a passage of a novel. Would a teacher of writing give it to a class as an example of what not to do?

again.instructions: `chapter` is a passage of a novel. Would a reader who has finished the book come back to read this passage again?

aloud.instructions: `chapter` is a passage of a novel. Would it be a pleasure to read aloud?

skip.instructions: `chapter` is a passage of a novel. How would a reader go through it?
criteria: A reader would read every word of this passage
A reader would skim some paragraphs of this passage
A reader would skip ahead to where something happens

lost.instructions: `chapter` is a passage of a novel. How far would it take a reader in?
criteria: A reader would stay aware of reading words on a page
A reader would follow this passage with interest
A reader would forget where they are while reading this passage

stop.instructions: `chapter` is a passage of a novel. Reaching the end of it, would a reader rather go on reading than stop for the day?

audience.instructions: `chapter` is a passage of a novel. Whom is it written for?

criteria.wide: The widest public, to pass the time
criteria.literary: Readers who read for the writing

remarks: The check of the behavioural questions, the test of ornament: the middle passage as it is, told dull and told overdone.
